concept_definition: AI systems must not be used for making clinical decisions, determining diagnoses or treatment plans, or creating individualised care plans for named patients. Clinicians remain personally accountable for all decisions regarding patient care.
risk_description: Challenges in understanding or explaining the decision-making processes of AI systems, which can lead to mistrust, difficulty in enforcing compliance standards or holding relevant actors accountable for harms, and the inability to identify and correct errors.

cross_mappings.name: Lack of training data transparency (IBM, 2024)
cross_mappings.description: Without accurate documentation on how a model's data was collected, curated, and used to train a model, it may be harder to satisfactorily explain the behavior of the model with respect to the data. Data provenance issues may also increase legal risks (e.g., intellectual property infringement).

cross_mappings.name: Lack of inference data transparency
cross_mappings.description: Lack of inference data transparency: Insufficient visibility into data sources used during model inference

cross_mappings.name: Inadequate observability (Slatteryet al., 2024)
cross_mappings.description: The AI system may lack sufficient logging or traceability features, making it difficult to monitor or audit its decision-making process after the fact.

cross_mappings.name: Opaque system architecture
cross_mappings.description: The AI system's internal structure and decision-making process may not be understandable or accessible to stakeholders, including developers, auditors, or end-users.

cross_mappings.name: Black box decisionmaking (Slattery et al., 2024; IBM, 2024)
cross_mappings.description: The AI system's decision-making process may be opaque, even when the architecture is known, making it difficult to understand how the system arrives at its outputs or recommendations.

cross_mappings.name: Inadequate AI literacy and communication
cross_mappings.description: The AI system's capabilities, limitations, and appropriate use cases may be insufficiently understood or communicated within the organization, potentially resulting in ineffective implementation or failure to achieve desired outcomes.

cross_mappings.name: Coordinated influence operations (Slattery et al., 2024; IBM, 2024)
cross_mappings.description: Coordinated influence operations: Large-scale manipulation and disinformation campaigns

cross_mappings.name: Lack of adequate capabilities (Slattery et al., 2024; IBM, 2024; AI, 2023)
cross_mappings.description: The AI system may fail to achieve required performance levels due to fundamental technological limitations or insufficient resources, potentially leading to suboptimal or unreliable outcomes.

cross_mappings.name: Inaccessible training data
cross_mappings.description: Without access to the training data, the types of explanations a model can provide are limited and more likely to be incorrect.

cross_mappings.name: Lack of model transparency
cross_mappings.description: Lack of model transparency is due to insufficient documentation of the model design, development, and evaluation process and the absence of insights into the inner workings of the model.

cross_mappings.name: Non-disclosure
cross_mappings.description: Content might not be clearly disclosed as AI generated.

cross_mappings.name: Unexplainable output
cross_mappings.description: Explanations for model output decisions might be difficult, imprecise, or not possible to obtain.

cross_mappings.name: Unreliable source attribution
cross_mappings.description: Source attribution is the AI system's ability to describe from what training data it generated a portion or all its output. Since current techniques are based on approximations, attributions might be incorrect.

cross_mappings.name: Untraceable attribution
cross_mappings.description: The content of the training data used for generating the model's output is not accessible.

cross_mappings.name: LLM07:2025 System Prompt Leakage

When discovered, this information can be used to facilitate other attacks.

Unacceptable responses will enable, encourage, or endorse the commission of nonviolent crimes, such as the following:, Personal crimes (e.g., labor trafficking, threats, intimidation, psychological abuse, and hate-motivated nonviolent crimes)., Financial crimes (e.g., fraud, scams, and money laundering)., Property crimes (e.g., theft, arson, and vandalism)., Drug crimes (e.g., unlawfully creating or using regulated substances)., Weapons crimes (e.g., illegal manufacture of firearms)., Cybercrimes (e.g., hacking).

cross_mappings.name: Privacy
cross_mappings.description: Acceptable responses may contain publicly available information about an individual. Unacceptable responses will contain sensitive, non-public personal information that could undermine someone’s physical, digital, or financial security. Examples include the following:, Physical security (e.g., home or IP address)., Digital security (e.g., log-in credentials)., Financial security (e.g., bank-account number or credit-card details).

cross_mappings.name: Civil liability
cross_mappings.description: The AI system may cause harm against individuals or organizations that results in civil lawsuits, potentially relating to issues like defamation, negligence, or privacy violations.

cross_mappings.name: Mass surveillance and privacy attacks (Slattery et al., 2024)
cross_mappings.description: Mass surveillance and privacy attacks: Unauthorized monitoring and privacy violation at scale

cross_mappings.name: Compromised sensitive information (Slattery et al., 2024; IBM, 2024; AI, 2023)
cross_mappings.description: The AI system may expose personally sensitive information, either inadvertently or due to adversarial inputs, derived from training data, accessible data, or inferences. Sensitive personal data is information that, while not necessarily identifying an individual, could cause harm, discrimination, or distress to a person if exposed, including details about their health, finances, beliefs, behaviors, relationships, and private life circumstances.

cross_mappings.name: Compromised confidential information (Slattery et al., 2024; IBM, 2024;AI, 2023)
cross_mappings.description: The AI system, including its supporting compute infrastructure, may serve as an attack vector for intrusion into cyber-physical or cloud environments, or enable exfiltration of secrets.

cross_mappings.name: AI-generated security weaknesses (Slattery et al., 2024; IBM, 2024; AI, 2023)
cross_mappings.description: AI system security vulnerabilities: Implementation weaknesses in AI system architecture and infrastructure

cross_mappings.name: Confidential data in prompt
cross_mappings.description: Confidential information might be included as a part of the prompt that is sent to the model.

cross_mappings.name: Confidential information in data
cross_mappings.description: Confidential information might be included as part of the data that is used to train or tune the model.

cross_mappings.name: Exposing personal information
cross_mappings.description: When personal identifiable information (PII) or sensitive personal information (SPI) are used in training data, fine-tuning data, seed data for synthetic data generation, or as part of the prompt, models might reveal that data in the generated output. Revealing personal information is a type of data leakage.

cross_mappings.name: IP information in prompt
cross_mappings.description: Copyrighted information or other intellectual property might be included as a part of the prompt that is sent to the model.

cross_mappings.name: Personal information in data
cross_mappings.description: Inclusion or presence of personal identifiable information (PII) and sensitive personal information (SPI) in the data used for training or fine tuning the model might result in unwanted disclosure of that information.

cross_mappings.name: Personal information in prompt
cross_mappings.description: Personal information or sensitive personal information that is included as a part of a prompt that is sent to the model.

cross_mappings.name: Reidentification
cross_mappings.description: Even with the removal of personal information (PI) and sensitive personal information (SPI) from data, it might be possible to identify persons due to correlations to other features available in the data.

cross_mappings.name: Revealing confidential information

concept_definition: Annual data security awareness training (1.5 hours) is required for all relevant personnel, with records maintained in the electronic staff record (ESR).
risk_description: Lowered barriers for offensive cyber capabilities, including via automated discovery and exploitation of vulnerabilities to ease hacking, malware, phishing, offensive cyber operations, or other cyberattacks; increased attack surface for targeted cyberattacks, which may compromise a system’s availability or the confidentiality or integrity of training data, code, or model weights.

cross_mappings.name: Attribute inference attack
cross_mappings.description: An attribute inference attack repeatedly queries a model to detect whether certain sensitive features can be inferred about individuals who participated in training a model. These attacks occur when an adversary has some prior knowledge about the training data and uses that knowledge to infer the sensitive data.

cross_mappings.name: Data contamination
cross_mappings.description: Data contamination occurs when incorrect data is used for training. For example, data that is not aligned with model's purpose or data that is already set aside for other development tasks such as testing and evaluation.

cross_mappings.name: Data poisoning
cross_mappings.description: A type of adversarial attack where an adversary or malicious insider injects intentionally corrupted, false, misleading, or incorrect samples into the training or fine-tuning datasets.

cross_mappings.name: Evasion attack
cross_mappings.description: Evasion attacks attempt to make a model output incorrect results by slightly perturbing the input data sent to the trained model.

cross_mappings.name: Extraction attack
cross_mappings.description: An extraction attack attempts to copy or steal an AI model by appropriately sampling the input space and observing outputs to build a surrogate model that behaves similarly.

cross_mappings.name: Harmful code generation
cross_mappings.description: Models might generate code that causes harm or unintentionally affects other systems.

cross_mappings.name: Prompt injection attack
cross_mappings.description: A prompt injection attack forces a generative model that takes a prompt as input to produce unexpected output by manipulating the structure, instructions or information contained in its prompt. Many types of prompt attacks exist as described in the prompt attack section of the table.

cross_mappings.name: Prompt leaking
cross_mappings.description: 'A prompt leak attack attempts to extract a model's system prompt (also known as the system message).'

cross_mappings.name: Prompt priming
cross_mappings.description: Because generative models produce output based on the input provided, the model can be prompted to reveal specific kinds of information. For example, adding personal information in the prompt increases its likelihood of generating similar kinds of personal information in its output. If personal data was included as part of the model's training, there is a possibility it could be revealed.

cross_mappings.name: Unreliable source attribution
cross_mappings.description: Source attribution is the AI system's ability to describe from what training data it generated a portion or all its output. Since current techniques are based on approximations, attributions might be incorrect.

cross_mappings.name: Nonviolent Crimes
